title: Trump Makes Closing Midterm Pitch at Lincoln Memorial on Eve of Election Day
dek: The president ends a 28-stop midterm blitz in Washington with a closing argument on the eve of Tuesday's vote, as an endorsement switch in Michigan reshapes a key Senate race.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The U.S. Capitol, west front (file photo)

keyPoints: President Trump will deliver his closing argument on the midterms at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday afternoon, a White House official said, according to NBC News.

Trump held the final rally of a 28-stop midterm blitz on Sunday in Salina, Kansas, where Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a tougher-than-expected challenge from Democrat Adam Hamilton, NBC reported.
NBC's latest poll puts Trump's approval at 40%. Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Mike Rogers over Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in the Michigan Senate race on Sunday.

Vice President JD Vance held a rally in upstate New York on Sunday and was headed to Ohio, NBC reported. The Trump administration also asked the Supreme Court on Monday to intervene in a California voter-citizenship dispute.
body:
President Donald Trump will deliver his closing argument on the midterm elections on Monday afternoon at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool in Washington, a White House official said. The Associated Press reported that the event places his campaign pitch at a site where his slow and costly repair work has drawn criticism. Forbes reported the reflecting pool remains closed to the public while repairs continue.

## The final stretch

Trump held the final rally of a 28-stop midterm blitz on Sunday in Salina, Kansas, according to NBC News. The president's rally schedule had been near-daily as Election Day approached, NPR reported. NBC's latest poll has his approval at 40%.

Vice President JD Vance attacked Democratic candidates at a New York rally on Sunday, calling one candidate an "a--hole," and was traveling next to Ohio, NBC reported.

## Michigan Senate shake-up

Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., endorsed Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers over her Democratic primary rival, Abdul El-Sayed, on Sunday, NBC reported. The endorsement came after Stevens was asked not to join a campaign event with El-Sayed because of their dispute over positions on Israel. A Michigan voter interviewed by NBC said the endorsement reaffirmed her vote for Rogers.

## Courts and voting

The Justice Department asked the Supreme Court on Monday to require California to separate ballots that officials say may have been cast by people who are not U.S. citizens, NBC reported. The federal government alleges that about 20,000 people registered to vote may be ineligible, and lower courts rejected the Justice Department's last-minute attempt to intervene.

## What to watch on Election Day

Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3. Control of the Senate is among the races most closely watched, and the Michigan contest drew national attention after the Stevens endorsement. Trump's 40% approval rating in NBC's latest poll sets the backdrop for the closing message, NBC reported. The AP and NPR accounts both describe the final weeks as a near-daily rally schedule, and the closing event in Washington marks the end of that run.

No results are reported in this story. Vote counts and race calls will be added as official returns come in.
